# Trill's swift-mosh copy

Upstream: https://github.com/wiedymi/swift-mosh
Revision: 966bd6fc9c7e4a7cf0ff514e313ca1e456e45494
License: MIT, included in LICENSE and Trill’s bundled acknowledgements.

Local functional changes:

- Transport clock privacy: `TransportClock.nowMs()` subtracts a lazily initialized process-local uptime origin and adds 1 (zero is used as a sentinel upstream). The monotonic timebase is retained for deadlines, RTT, and retransmission. Encrypted Mosh packet timestamps now describe elapsed time inside this process; no raw device uptime is transmitted. The privacy manifest declares 35F9.1 for timing within the app. Snapshot persistence across process lifetimes is not used by Trill; revisit the clock contract if adding that capability.

- Peer liveness generation: `MoshClientSession.peerResponseCount` is a public, actor-isolated, read-only `UInt64` starting at zero. It advances (with wrapping arithmetic) once per nonempty, successfully decoded and protocol-valid accepted transport instruction, before remote-state deduplication. ACK-only replies, empty diffs, and fresh transport packets repeating an already applied remote state count even when no host operations are emitted. ACKs are accepted before checking whether a diff's base state is available, so those responses also count. Malformed packets/instructions, authentication failures, protocol-version mismatches, empty datagrams, and empty assembled payloads do not advance it. Authentication follows `useNetworkCrypto` (enabled by default); the explicit plaintext test configuration does not authenticate traffic.

The liveness counter survives suspend/resume and transport restart on the same session actor. It is not included in snapshots; a newly restored actor starts at zero. Callers can read a baseline immediately before resume, then wait for inequality. The transport engine authenticates and filters wrong-direction and stale/replayed packet sequences before delivering completed instructions; its incoming sequence watermark is retained across suspend/resume. Freshly sequenced retransmissions of the same instruction can count; replayed ciphertext below the watermark cannot. This is accepted peer traffic, not a challenge/response guarantee of freshness: a previously unseen delayed authenticated packet may still advance it. Fragmented instructions count once on completed assembly, not once per datagram.

- Abortable startup: `MoshClientSession.start()` retains its engine before awaiting endpoint startup, allowing `stop()` to cancel a pending UDP start (including application resume). State and engine-identity checks after startup and snapshot restoration reject obsolete completion with the existing `TransportError.cancelled`. Startup error cleanup closes only its own engine and returns to idle only while it still owns the attempt; late success or failure cannot revive a stopped session or overwrite a replacement. Shutdown detaches its engine and host streams before awaiting endpoint stop. Starts during `.stopping` throw the existing `MoshSessionError.notStarted`; overlapping stop calls leave completion to the first caller. The receive loop's peer-shutdown acknowledgement path still performs normal cleanup.

- Bounded incoming data: `NetworkDatagramEndpoint` retains at most 64 queued datagrams before authentication, dropping the oldest when full. `MoshFragmentAssembly` resets and rejects an assembly exceeding 16 MiB, accounting for replacement fragments without counting duplicate bytes twice. `MoshCompressionCodec` rejects decoded output exceeding 16 MiB before appending each chunk, for both zlib and Apple Compression paths. These limits bound individual queues/messages; they are not a total process-memory budget. Regression tests cover queue eviction, fragment limits and reset, duplicate accounting, and excessive decompression.

Regressions cover device-uptime privacy and encrypted in-memory peer responses: ACK-only/repeated/no-op state responses, invalid traffic leaving an existing count unchanged, empty payload and replay/direction filtering, and count plus replay-watermark preservation through suspend/resume. Fake-endpoint startup regressions cover cancellation of initial start and resume, late success after stop, late success/failure after replacement, start/repeated-stop overlap during pending shutdown, and failed-start cleanup racing a new startup. Upstream unit and transport tests are retained. Network-server integration tests remain opt-in.

The app and tools/TransportProbe both use this copy. When updating upstream, review these changes and the linked SDK privacy API inventory before replacing the directory.

This copy tracks local changes in this file and Git; there is no separately maintained swift-mosh patch file.
